q.t: Solve x + y = 10 and x − y = 2. Find x.
q.e: Add the equations: 2x = 12, so x = 6.

q.t: Solve x + y = 10 and x − y = 2. Find y.
q.e: Subtract the second from the first: 2y = 8, so y = 4.

q.t: A pair of linear equations has a₁/a₂ ≠ b₁/b₂. The lines…
q.e: Unequal ratios mean the lines have different slopes, so they must cross — and two straight lines cross only once.

q.t: What are the lines 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + 6y = 10?
q.e: The second is just the first doubled, so it is the very same line; every point on it is a solution.

q.t: What are the lines 2x + 3y = 7 and 4x + 6y = 9?
q.e: 2/4 = 3/6 but ≠ 7/9: same slope, different line, so they never meet.

q.t: If x = 2 in 3x + 2y = 12, find y.
Is (2, 1) a solution of 3x − y = 5?
q.e: Put x = 2, y = 1 into the left side: 3 × 2 − 1 = 5, which matches.

q.t: 5 pens and 3 pencils cost ₹50. A pen costs ₹7. What does a pencil cost (in ₹)?
q.e: 5 × 7 = 35, so the 3 pencils cost 15; one pencil is 5.

q.t: Two numbers add to 25 and differ by 7. Find the larger.
q.e: Add the two facts: 2 × larger = 32, so the larger is 16.

q.t: kx + 2y = 5 and 3x + y = 1 have a unique solution when…
q.e: Unique solution needs k/3 ≠ 2/1, i.e. k ≠ 6. If k = 6 the lines are parallel.

q.t: For what k do x + 2y = 3 and (k + 1)x + 6y = 5 have no solution?
q.e: No solution needs 1/(k + 1) = 2/6, so k + 1 = 3 and k = 2. Then 2/6 ≠ 3/5, so the lines really are parallel.

q.t: For what k do 2x + 3y = 7 and kx + 9y = 21 have infinitely many solutions?
Solve 2x + y = 7 and x − y = 2. Find x.
q.e: Add: 3x = 9, so x = 3 (then y = 1).

q.t: Solve 3x − 4y = 10 and 4x + 3y = 5. Find y.
A father is 3 times as old as his son. In 10 years he will be twice as old. Find the son’s age now.
A fraction becomes 1/2 if 1 is added to both its numerator and denominator, and 1/3 if 1 is taken from both. Find it.
A two-digit number has digit sum 9. Reversing the digits adds 27. Find the number.
q.e: Reversed − original = 9(b − a) = 27, so b − a = 3. With a + b = 9: a = 3, b = 6.

q.t: Where do the lines x = 2 and y = 3 meet?
q.e: x = 2 is every point with x-coordinate 2; y = 3 every point with y-coordinate 3. Only (2, 3) is on both.

q.t: Find the area of the triangle formed by x + y = 4 and the two axes.
q.e: The line meets the axes at (4, 0) and (0, 4), so the triangle has legs 4 and 4: ½ × 4 × 4 = 8.

q.t: 2 chairs and 3 tables cost ₹2900; 3 chairs and 2 tables cost ₹2600. Find the price of a table (in ₹).
q.e: Add: 5 chairs + 5 tables = 5500, so c + t = 1100. Subtract: t − c = 300. So t = 700.

q.t: Solve 3/x + 2/y = 12 and 2/x + 3/y = 13. Find y.
q.e: Let u = 1/x, v = 1/y: 3u + 2v = 12, 2u + 3v = 13. Adding gives u + v = 5, subtracting gives u − v = −1; so v = 3 and y = 1/3.

q.t: A boat goes 24 km upstream and 36 km downstream in 7 hours, and 36 km upstream and 48 km downstream in 10 hours. Find its speed in still water.
q.e: With u = upstream and d = downstream speeds, 24/u + 36/d = 7 and 36/u + 48/d = 10 give u = 6, d = 12. Still-water speed is their average: 9.

q.t: Five years ago A was three times as old as B. Ten years from now A will be twice as old as B. Find A’s present age.
q.e: A − 5 = 3(B − 5) gives A = 3B − 10; A + 10 = 2(B + 10) gives A = 2B + 10. So B = 20 and A = 50.

q.t: A person travels 360 km partly by train and partly by car. With 240 km by train it takes 7 h; with 300 km by train it takes 6.5 h. Find the train’s speed.
q.e: Let a = 1/train speed, b = 1/car speed: 240a + 120b = 7 and 300a + 60b = 6.5. Solving gives a = 1/60, b = 1/40.

q.t: A two-digit number is 4 times its digit sum and twice the product of its digits. Find it.
q.e: 10a + b = 4(a + b) gives b = 2a. Then 10a + 2a = 2a(2a), so 12a = 4a² and a = 3, b = 6.

q.t: If a rectangle’s length grows by 3 m and breadth shrinks by 2 m, its area falls by 8 m². If the length shrinks by 2 m and breadth grows by 3 m, the area rises by 12 m². Find the area.
q.e: Expanding: −2l + 3b = −2 and 3l − 2b = 18. Solving gives l = 10, b = 6.

q.t: Find the area of the triangle formed by the lines y = x, x + y = 6 and the x-axis.
q.e: The lines meet at (3, 3); they cut the x-axis at (0, 0) and (6, 0). Base 6, height 3: ½ × 6 × 3.

q.t: A fraction’s numerator and denominator add to 12. If 3 is added to the denominator, it becomes 1/2. Find the fraction.
q.e: x + y = 12 and 2x = y + 3. Adding: 3x = 15, so x = 5, y = 7.

q.t: For what value of k do kx + 3y = k − 3 and 12x + ky = k have no solution?
q.e: No solution needs k/12 = 3/k, so k² = 36, k = ±6. But k = 6 makes 3/6 = 3/6 too (same line), so k = −6.

q.t: Solve 41x + 53y = 135 and 53x + 41y = 147. Find x.
q.e: Add: 94(x + y) = 282, so x + y = 3. Subtract: 12(x − y) = 12, so x − y = 1. Hence x = 2.

q.t: Solve 10/(x + y) + 2/(x − y) = 4 and 15/(x + y) − 5/(x − y) = −2. Find x.
A car drives a fixed distance at a steady speed. 5 km/h faster, it would take 3 hours less; 5 km/h slower, it would take 5 hours more. Find the distance.
q.e: (v + 5)(t − 3) = vt gives 5t − 3v = 15; (v − 5)(t + 5) = vt gives v − t = 5. So t = 15, v = 20.

q.t: A two-digit number plus the number with its digits reversed is 66, and the digits differ by 2. How many such numbers are there?
q.e: 11(a + b) = 66 gives a + b = 6; with a difference of 2 the digits are 4 and 2 — so 42 and 24 both work.

q.t: A taxi charges a fixed amount plus a rate per km. 10 km costs ₹105 and 15 km costs ₹155. What does 25 km cost (in ₹)?
q.e: 5 more km cost ₹50, so ₹10 per km; fixed charge = 105 − 100 = 5. For 25 km: 5 + 250.

q.t: 2 women and 5 men finish a job in 2 days; 4 women and 1 man take 4 days. How many days would one man alone take?
q.e: Daily work: 2w + 5m = 1/2 and 4w + m = 1/4. Double the first and subtract: 9m = 3/4, so m = 1/12.

q.t: A father’s age plus twice his son’s is 70. Twice the father’s age plus the son’s is 95. Find the son’s age.
q.e: Adding: 3(F + S) = 165, so F + S = 55; subtracting: F − S = 25. So S = 15.

q.t: For what k do 2x + 3y = 4 and (k + 2)x + 6y = 3k + 2 have infinitely many solutions?
q.e: Need 2/(k + 2) = 3/6 = 4/(3k + 2). The first gives k = 2; check the second: 3k + 2 = 8 ✓.

q.t: Two items are sold: first at 10% profit and second at 5% loss, total ₹1215; or first at 5% loss and second at 10% profit, total ₹1245. Find the cost price of the first item (in ₹).
Two cars start from P and Q, 120 km apart. Driving the same way they meet in 6 hours; driving towards each other they meet in 1 h 12 min. Find the faster car’s speed.
q.e: Same direction: a − b = 120/6 = 20. Towards: a + b = 120/1.2 = 100. So a = 60.

q.t: Solve x/a − y/b = 0 and ax + by = a² + b².
q.e: The first gives y = bx/a. Put it in the second: ax + b²x/a = a² + b², so x(a² + b²)/a = a² + b², giving x = a and then y = b.
